;Law and crime
*[[LGBT rights in the Cook Islands]]
**The [[Cook Islands]] announces it will retain its ban on [[Homosexuality|homosexual]] [[Gay sexual practices|practices by men]] and that it will be [[Lesbian sexual practices|extended to women]] as well. Homosexuals face up to seven years of imprisonment on the islands. [https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/402530/cook-islands-retains-ban-on-homosexuality (Radio New Zealand)]
*[[Crime in Italy]]
**Three [[firefighter]]s are killed while two others and a [[law enforcement in Italy|policeman]] are injured after an explosion at an abandoned farm building in [[Quargnento]], [[Piedmont]], [[Italy]]. The explosion was caused by two bombs placed in the building. [https://www.foxnews.com/world/italy-firefighters-killed-explosion (Fox News)]
*[[Murder of Ana Kriégel]]
**An [[Irish people|Irish]] judge sentences two 15-year-old boys to jail for the 2018 murder of 14-year-old Ana Kriégel in suburban [[Dublin]]. The boys were 13-years-old at the time they murdered her and are the youngest people convicted of murder in [[Republic of Ireland|Ireland]]. They have not been named due to their age. One boy was sentenced to [[life imprisonment|life in detention]] to be reviewed after twelve years—he was also sentenced to eight years for [[sexual assault]] to run concurrently with the murder sentence. The other boy was sentenced to 15 years in prison, but his sentence will be reviewed after eight years instead of twelve. Her parents said that "justice has been served for Ana", but about the sentences that "forever is not long enough". [https://www.rte.ie/news/ireland/2019/1105/1088699-kriegel-sentencing/ (RTE News and Current Affairs)] [https://www.rte.ie/news/courts/2019/1105/1088828-ana-kriegel/ (RTE News and Current Affairs<sub>2</sub>)]
*[[Impeachment inquiry into Donald Trump]]
**[[Gordon Sondland]], the [[United States Ambassador to the European Union]], reverses his previous testimony, admitting to a ''[[quid pro quo]]'' in the withholding of military aid for [[Ukraine]]. [https://www.nytimes.com/2019/11/05/us/politics/impeachment-trump.html (''The New York Times'')]

;Politics and elections
*[[2019 Virginia elections]], [[2019 Kentucky gubernatorial election]]
**Democrats win majorities in both houses of the [[Virginia]] [[Virginia General Assembly|General Assembly]] ([[Senate of Virginia|Senate]] and [[Virginia House of Delegates|House]]), resulting in Democratic [[Government trifecta|trifecta]] control of the [[Governor of Virginia|governorship]] and General Assembly for the first time since 1993. Democratic [[Attorney General of Kentucky|Kentucky Attorney General]] [[Andy Beshear]] defeats Republican incumbent [[Matt Bevin]] to win the [[Governor of Kentucky|governorship]] of Kentucky. [https://www.vox.com/policy-and-politics/2019/11/5/20944109/virginia-elections-legislature-results-democrats (''Vox'')] [https://www.washingtonpost.com/polls-open-in-virginia-balance-of-power-in-state-government-is-at-stake/2019/11/05/bdb57972-ff5b-11e9-8501-2a7123a38c58_story.html (''The Washington Post'')] [https://edition.cnn.com/2019/11/05/politics/virginia-election-democrats-control/index.html (CNN)]
